faq: Which chart libraries do you use?
Usually Chart.js, Recharts or ECharts, depending on your stack. We choose one that is light, accessible and easy for your developers to maintain.
Do you decide which charts to build?
We suggest them. Send us the questions you want answered and we propose the chart type for each. You approve the list before we build, so nothing is wasted.
Can you connect to Google Analytics or Stripe data?
Yes, through their official APIs, if you give us access as a collaborator. We confirm what data is available first, because some tools limit what they expose.
Are the numbers checked for accuracy?
Yes. We compare each chart against your raw data on a sample and share the check with you. We cannot fix numbers that are wrong at the source, but we point them out.
desc:
Dashboard charts and reports for SaaS data turn the numbers in your database into answers people can read at a glance. Ecom Swift LLC chooses the right chart for each question and builds it into your app with filters, date ranges and readable colors.

## Why do dashboard charts and reports matter?

Dashboard charts and reports matter because raw data does not answer questions on its own. A table of ten thousand rows hides the pattern that one line chart shows in a second. Good charts help people see growth, spot drops and compare groups without doing sums in a spreadsheet.

Poor charts do the opposite. A pie chart with twelve slices, a bar chart with an unlabeled axis or colors that look the same to some viewers all create doubt rather than clarity.

## How clear reporting supports decisions

People act on what they can understand quickly. A founder deciding where to focus needs to see which plans grow and which stall. A support lead assigning staff needs to see when requests peak. When those answers sit inside the product, nobody has to request a special report from a developer.

The mechanism is simple: fewer steps between a question and an answer means more questions get asked. Date ranges, filters and comparisons to the previous period let users explore without leaving the page. Customers who see their own results clearly also tend to value the product more, because the benefit is visible every time they log in.

## What good reports and charts include

- Charts chosen for the question: lines for change over time, bars for comparisons, pie only for few parts of a whole.
- Clear titles that state what is shown and for which period.
- Axis labels, units and legends that need no explanation.
- A date range filter and filters by plan, region or status.
- Tooltips that show exact values on hover or tap.
- A summary table beside the charts for people who want the figures.
- A comparison with the previous period.
- Colors that stay readable for people with color vision differences.
- Saved filter views and downloadable chart data.
- A print-friendly layout for meetings.

## How we work

We start with your questions, not with chart types. You tell us what you want to know, such as weekly growth, best-selling plans or the busiest hours, and we list the data needed for each answer. We agree which chart suits each one and where it will live in your app.

Then we write the queries that shape the data, build the charts with a charting library that fits your front-end, and add filters and tooltips. We compare the figures on screen with the source data, so what users see matches what your database holds. The Basic package delivers a few charts with a date filter. Standard adds a full report page with a summary table, filters and period comparison. Premium builds several report pages with saved views, data download, a print layout and handover notes.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Begin with the question each chart must answer.
- Label axes and state the time period.
- Use few colors and keep them consistent between charts.
- Let users change the date range.
- Check the totals against the source data.

**Avoid:**
- Using a chart type because it looks impressive.
- Cutting a bar chart's axis so small differences look large.
- Packing many series into one chart.
- Relying on color alone to separate lines.
- Showing numbers without saying what period they cover.

## Who this is for

This service suits SaaS teams whose customers ask for reports and usage charts. It suits founders who currently pull numbers by hand each week, and product teams adding an analytics tab to an existing app. It also helps teams whose current charts are confusing and need a cleaner redesign.

## What we need from you

Send a list of the questions you want answered, and any existing reports or spreadsheets you use today. Tell us where the data lives and share a test copy of it.

Give us developer access to your code repository, and we will build the charts inside your project. We never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until the charts are live.
